key_insight: CAM-B3LYP captures pentacene–buckminsterfullerene charge-transfer energetics much more reliably than B3LYP or DFTB, with results close to an optimally tuned range-separated hybrid benchmark.
engineering_relevance: For organic photovoltaic interface design, the choice of electronic-structure method strongly affects predicted excitations and can change the apparent donor–acceptor charge-transfer alignment by about 1 eV.
method: Compared four pentacene/C60 interface models with different donor–acceptor geometries.
Computed local excited states and charge-transfer states using TDDFT with CAM-B3LYP and B3LYP.
Compared against DFTB and reference results from optimally tuned range-separated hybrid functionals.
evidence_signal: Across all models, CAM-B3LYP produced charge-transfer energies close to OPT-wB97XD, while B3LYP and DFTB underestimated the charge-transfer state by roughly 1 eV.
watch_item: B3LYP and DFTB may mis-rank or misplace charge-transfer states at organic interfaces, so they are risky choices for quantitative device screening.
paper_title: Local and Charge-Transfer Excitation of Pentacene-Buckminsterfullerene complexes
